claims.claim: The 0.01% figure = 8 proactive arrests in September out of ~80,000 registered draft evaders and deserters
claims.verified_figure: IDF: 8 successful proactive arrests (of 15 attempts) in September 2026. Denominator ~80,000 registered evaders+deserters per High Court proceedings (~82,000 in some reports). 8 / 80,000 = 0.010%; 8 / 82,000 = 0.0098%.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: '8 משתמטים ועריקים נעצרו ... מתוך 15 ניסיונות למעצרים יזומים, מדובר על 0.01% בלבד מתוך כ-80,000'
claims.note: Arithmetic checks out exactly within rounding. The 0.01% is ynet's own derivation (IDF supplied the 8/15; the ~80,000 stock comes from the court proceedings), not a figure the IDF published. Note it divides a one-month flow by a cumulative stock — a legitimate 'monthly enforcement rate' framing, but a period-mixed ratio that should be read as such.

claims.claim: 0.01% of draft evaders and deserters were 'caught' (נתפסו) in September
claims.verified_figure: Per the same IDF clarification, in addition to the 8 proactive arrests, 212 draft evaders were arrested at border crossings between 1 and 22 September (163 Haredi). Counting all reported captures (>=220, with the border tally covering only 22 days), the September capture rate is >=~0.27% of ~80,000 — roughly 27x the headline figure.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: Coverage of the same story (ynet/ynetnews snippets) reports both the 212 border-crossing arrests and the 8 of 15 proactive arrests; the headline uses only the latter.
claims.note: The 0.01% is correctly computed but is attached to the wrong meaning: it measures *proactive Military Police raids* only, while the headline's 'נתפסו' (were caught) reads as all captures. The IDF's own figures for the same month include 212 border-crossing arrests, which the headline omits. Directionally the point stands (enforcement is minuscule either way: ~0.3% vs 0.01%), which is why this is not 'contradicted'; but the specific number does not mean what the headline says. Article body unreachable (EGRESS_BLOCKED) — judged the headline against IDF figures surfaced in search snippets; the body appears (per snippets) to carry both figures, so the divergence is headline-level. The police-vs-IDF blame for the Modi'in riot in the second half of the headline is event logistics/framing and out of scope.
